Financial implications of the risk or opportunity (Indicate positive or negative implications)
Health and occupational safety of own workforce

The chemical manufacturing industry involves hazardous processes. Inadequate occupational health and safety measures can lead to workplace accidents, health issues, regulatory penalties, employee dissatisfaction, and reputational damage. Moreover, maintaining a safe work environment is a legal and ethical imperative.

Regular safety audits and compliance with OSHA/Indian Factories Act safety trainings, use of personal protective equipment and automation in hazardous zones, real-time safety monitoring systems, emergency preparedness drills and health surveillance programs
Developing new and sustainable products helps the business respond to evolving customer preferences and regulatory trends, offering differentiation and positioning in future-ready markets.
Sourcing from ethical and environmentally responsible suppliers helps mitigate reputational, legal, and supply chain continuity risks, especially in sensitive industries.

Strengthening supplier ESG audits, deploying traceability platforms, and comprehensively integrating ESG-related clauses within procurement policies will help ensure responsible sourcing across the supply chain.
Creating and transparently reporting economic value strengthens trust among investors, governments, and communities, while demonstrating contribution to inclusive growth and development.
Adoption of AI and emerging technologies can improve operational efficiency, enhance data-driven decision-making, and drive innovation across business processes.

Financial implications of the risk or opportunity (Indicate positive or negative implications)
High water consumption poses operational and regulatory risks, particularly in water- stressed areas, and increases vulnerability to physical climate risks.

Implementing water efficiency technologies, establishing recycling systems, and actively participating in watershed restoration initiatives can significantly reduce water consumption and support long-term water security.
Improper discharge of wastewater can lead to environmental pollution, regulatory non-compliance, and reputational damage, resulting in potential fines and operational disruptions.
Investing in advanced wastewater treatment systems, regular monitoring, and compliance audits can ensure safe discharge and reduce environmental impact.

High water dependency for operations in water-stressed geographies makes the business vulnerable to water scarcity, seasonal variability, and regulatory limits on industrial withdrawal. Increasing stakeholder and regulatory scrutiny on freshwater use also poses reputational risk.

Implementation of Zero Liquid Discharge (ZLD) systems in facilities, increase in water recycling and reuse through ETP/RO systems, shift to rainwater harvesting and groundwater recharge initiatives, sourcing water from sustainable and alternate sources
Health and safety of workers in the value chain
Health and safety of contractors has implications on legal compliance, productivity, workforce morale, and employer reputation, especially in high-hazard sectors.
The OHS system covers 100% of workers at offices and depots manufacturing, and R&D facilities. Occupational safety includes a stringent work permit system, SOP adherence, and use of PIDs
Gender equality and equal pay for work of equal value at own workforce

Diverse and inclusive teams have been shown to perform better, make more innovative decisions, and improve overall productivity. Further, gender pay gaps and inequality can lead to reputational damage, consumer boycotts, and negative media coverage.
Regular reviews and benchmarking conducted to identify and close pay gaps, promote fairness, and equal opportunity across our workforce

Details of the initiative (Web-link, if any, may be provided along-with summary)

1 EcoScale tool The EcoScale tool provides a more comprehensive assessment of chemical reactions through the E-factor optimization approach, by incorporating factors such as cost, safety, environmental impact, and resource efficiency. This offers a practical and accessible method for assessing the sustainability of chemical processes in organic chemistry and for making informed decisions that contribute to more sustainable and cost-effective chemical production. Improved recyclability and waste reduction at the product design stage
Details of the initiative (Web-link, if any, may be provided along- with summary)
2 Purchase of Hybrid power This year, we purchased hybrid (solar and wind) energy for our manufacturing plants in Panoli and Jambusar areas Increased share of renewable energy

3 Rooftop solar installation We set up rooftop solar plants starting with Jambusar in June 2022 and later in our Udaipur premises from October 2022. We continue to benefit from these installations in the form of increased share of renewable energy in the total electricity mix. Reduced dependence on fossil fuel electricity at Jambusar plant and Udaipur R&D centre

4 Fuel Switching initiative In December 2023, we switched from FO/LDO to LNG in boilers at our Panoli and Jambusar plants. This financial year, we have accrued benefits in the form of reduced non GHG air emissions recorded at plant sites due to fuel switching. Nearly 50% reduction in SOx emissions from last FY
5 Installation of RO systems We have set up an RO plant of 650 KLD capacity at our manufacturing facility in Jambusar. 82,513 KL of freshwater consumption reduced

6 Smart infrastructure Motion sensor installations optimizing power consumption, optimization of HVAC chilled water circuits ensuring efficient cooling operations and AHU running hour adjustments optimizing air handling for energy saving. Energy conservation
7 Installation of PVC drift eliminators We have installed PVC drift eliminators to enhance the efficiency and performance of our cooling towers. Reduced water consumption in cooling towers

8 Development of low-carbon products Over the past 20 years, we have been strategically building a comprehensive biologicals portfolio, reinforcing our commitment to sustainable agricultural solutions. 7. Statement by director responsible for the business responsibility report, highlighting ESG related challenges, targets and achievements (listed entity has flexibility regarding the placement of this disclosure)

Sustainability continues to shape how PI Industries approaches growth, innovation and long-term value creation. These include increasing renewable energy share to 21%, alongside clearly defined goals, targets and measurable outcomes across priority areas in alignment with commitment to SBTi. In an environment where expectations from businesses are evolving rapidly, we remain focused on embedding responsible practices into our operations and decision-making. Over the year, we have made tangible progress in strengthening environmental performance across our manufacturing footprint. Our efforts towards renewable energy adoption have steadily increased its share in our overall energy mix, supporting our transition toward a lower-carbon future. Our water stewardship initiatives continue to deliver measurable improvements, with an overall reduction of 6% in freshwater withdrawal, supported by enhanced recycling, reuse and process efficiencies. In parallel, we have strengthened our approach to waste circularity, with an increase in recovery and co-processing rates across sites. During the year, we further enhanced our climate and environmental risk management framework through alignment with the Task Force on Climate-related Financial Disclosures (TCFD), including identification and assessment of climate risks and opportunities across our operations. We also initiated alignment with the Taskforce on Nature-related Financial Disclosures (TNFD), undertaking our first structured assessment of nature-related risks and dependencies as part of our broader natural capital approach. Building on this, we have undertaken focused biodiversity management initiatives across key sites, including greenbelt development at Panoli and agri-silvi models in Jambusar, contributing to ecosystem restoration and environmental resilience. These efforts reflect our recognition of natural capital as a core operational driver, with linkages across our value chain and will be progressively scaled as part of our TNFD journey.

Our focus on people extends beyond our workforce into areas where our operations can drive meaningful impact. We have initiated structured ESG engagement with suppliers, with 100% of key suppliers assessed on ESG parameters and improvement programs underway, while our community initiatives have positively impacted over 1.5 lakh beneficiaries during the year. These efforts are underpinned by a strong governance framework, with enhanced systems, controls and ESG data tracking across operations. As the external landscape evolves, we remain focused on scaling priority areas, including supplier ESG coverage, biodiversity, nature strategy and renewable energy adoption. At PI Industries, we see sustainability as a critical enabler of long-term competitiveness and resilience. With a sustained focus on execution, innovation and measurable outcomes, we remain committed to delivering meaningful progress for all our stakeholders. – Mr. Rajnish Sarna Joint Managing Director

Details of improvements in environmental and social impacts

Development and adoption of advanced technologies focused on improving process efficiency, reducing waste and emissions, enhancing water treatment and reuse and enabling safer, more sustainable product formulations. Investments in renewable energy, green chemistry and biological research have further supported the transition towards lower environmental impact and improved occupational safety outcomes.

This year, efforts focused on improving energy efficiency through advanced technologies and renewable energy adoption, alongside strengthening recycling, resource recovery and waste management systems. Investments in ESG infrastructure were enhanced to support sustainability and compliance, while OHS infrastructure was upgraded with smart systems and proactive measures to improve safety and mitigate risks.

The organization complies with Extended Producer Responsibility (EPR) requirements and has systems in place for the collection, recycling and disposal of plastic waste generated from sold products. A closed loop waste management approach has been adopted in line with circular economy principles. Plastic waste collection and recycling targets have been met consistently, as reflected on the Central Pollution Control Board portal.

E-waste is segregated at the designated waste management area within PI’s manufacturing facilities. The segregated e waste is subsequently handed over to an authorised third party E-waste recycler for processing and disposal.

Hazardous waste generated at PI’s owned facilities is segregated at source and managed through structured collection and storage systems. The majority of this waste is directed towards recycling through authorised recyclers and resource recovery from waste is channelised through authorised preprocessing and co-processing facilities. The remaining waste are disposed to approved Common Hazardous Waste Treatment Storage & Disposal Facilities (CHWTSDF). All waste streams are tracked in detail from generation to final disposal.

Waste streams such as biomedical waste and battery waste are managed in accordance with applicable statutory requirements; wherein biomedical waste is disposed through authorized common biomedical waste management facilities, battery waste is channelized to authorized recyclers, construction and demolition (C&D) waste, comprising largely of soil, is utilized within the premises to the extent feasible and remaining C&D waste, other non-hazardous waste like paper, wood, metal, glass, etc. is routed through respective authorized recyclers. Expired products received through the depot network are channelled to manufacturing plants for appropriate handling in accordance with approved waste management procedures.

Details: • Purchased Biomass based steam for Panoli cluster has resulted in substantial 14,178 MTCO₂e emissions reduction, strengthening the transition toward low carbon operations. In addition, fuel switching initiative implemented at plant sites during the previous financial year have contributed to a significant reduction in air emissions. • Renewable energy adoption has been implemented in a phased manner across operations through multiple pathways, including sourcing of solar power, deployment of hybrid renewable energy from third party provider and installation of roof-top solar system under the BOOT (Build Own Operate Transfer) model • New energy-efficient screw chillers at Panoli reduced power consumption by 10%, Variable Frequency Drive (VFD) installations on air compressors contributed a further 3% reduction and replacement of legacy compressors with advanced technology delivered 7.2% energy savings • Dry vacuum pumps replaced steam jet ejectors at both Panoli and Jambusar, reducing steam consumption by 6% and 5.2% respectively. • Optimisation of dry air generation plant settings at Jambusar achieved an 11% reduction in specific power consumption, instrument air compressor controls delivered a 9% improvement and a heat pump installation reduced steam consumption for hot water generation by 120 KL per month while generating 7,376 TR per month of chilled water. • 232kWp rooftop solar plant commissioned at Udaipur R&D under Phase 3 generates an estimated 2,05,732 KWh per year; automation of chiller pumps and return line circuits saved 105,169 kWh per year; and steam consumption reduction through process optimisation delivered fuel savings of 36,521 litres per year. • In addition, a hydro turbine–based energy recovery initiative for the Cooling Tower fan and expanded VFD coverage resulted in Reduce SPC of Pump from 0.48 KW/KL to 0.28 KW/KL are part of the broader continuous improvement roadmap to enhance energy productivity and operational resilience under strategic objectives • The Company is engaging with suppliers to strengthen Scope 3 emissions management This includes collection of fuel, energy and Product Carbon Footprint (PCF) data from suppliers. • The initiatives are focused on achieving long term emissions reduction across the value chain.
